chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Sniff the banafsjah (violet oil), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If people knew what was in the banafsjah, they would drink it with a slurping sound.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْبَنَفْسَجِ: Violet oil or essence, a fragrant substance used for scent and medicinal purposes.
key_terms.حَسْواً: Drinking with a slurping sound, indicating eagerness or thorough consumption.
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of violet oil (banafsjah) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the medicinal and spiritual virtue of *banafsjah* (violet oil), linking the Prophet’s declaration to Imam Ali’s recommendation, thereby establishing a chain of prophetic and imamic endorsement for its use. In Shia scholarly tradition, this reflects the broader concept of *tadawi* (healing) through natural means, where physical remedies are seen as manifestations of divine wisdom. The hyperbolic phrase 'consume it as one consumes water' emphasizes the urgency and high value of its benefits, encouraging believers to seek out and utilize such remedies for holistic well-being.
